evals.prompt: I have a workflow I repeat every sprint: pull the RHOAI release notes PDF from my downloads folder, extract the fixed-bug list, and post a summary to our team channel. Turn this into a skill following the repo conventions.
assertions: The output contains a YAML frontmatter block with name, description and metadata fields.
The proposed skill directory includes a '## When to use' section.
The skill description states when to trigger the skill, not just what it does.

evals.prompt: Review this skill draft for me: it is named 'MyCoolSkill', the description says 'helps with Jira', and the body jumps straight into steps with no title heading. What needs to change before I submit it to redhat-cop/skills?
assertions: The output flags that the skill name must be kebab-case and match the directory name.
The output flags that the description must say when to use the skill and stay under 500 characters.
The output flags the missing '# Title' H1 and '## When to use' section in the body.

evals.prompt: My skill keeps under-triggering — users ask for dashboards and the skill never fires. Its description is 'Builds dashboards.' Improve the description for better triggering accuracy.
assertions: The output proposes a description that enumerates concrete trigger phrases (e.g. 'dashboard', 'data visualization', 'metrics').
The output keeps the proposed description under 500 characters.
The output explains that the description is the primary triggering mechanism for skill discovery.
